sections.h2: What territory management settles before the selling starts
paras: Territory management answers one question in advance: for any given account, who is responsible. Split by geography, by segment, by product line or by a mixture of the three, and every hospital, lab or dealer belongs to exactly one rep who is measured on it.

Aura Business holds this in the territory and target management module. Accounts carry a territory, territories carry an owner and a target, and the reporting that follows, on pipeline, orders, collections and coverage, can be read territory by territory instead of as one company-wide figure.

For medical sales the segment split matters as much as the map. A government medical college, a corporate chain and a standalone nursing home in the same district buy in different ways, and it is reasonable for different reps to own them. The model allows that without leaving any account unowned.

sections.h2: What an undivided market costs you.
sections.lead: Overlap wastes money and looks unprofessional. Gaps are worse, because nobody notices them.

items.p: The purchase officer receives two quotations from the same company in a week, sometimes at different prices.
A district is assumed to be covered by whoever passes through it, so nobody calls there at all.

items.h: Targets set for the company, not the patch
items.p: One overall number hides a territory that has not grown in two years.
When an order comes in, two reps claim it because the account was never assigned.
You know which products sell but not which parts of the market buy them.
A territory changes hands and the new rep starts with a list of names and no context.

items.q: Can a territory be a segment rather than an area?
items.a: Yes. Territories can be drawn by geography, by customer segment such as government or corporate chains, or by product line, and an account is placed in the one that reflects who should own it.

items.q: Can two reps share an account?
items.a: The model is built around one owner per account so credit and follow-up are unambiguous. Where a specialist supports a sale, that involvement is recorded through visits and activity rather than by splitting ownership.
Role-based access decides that. The usual setup gives a rep their own accounts and gives managers and the owner a view across all territories on the dashboard.
Targets are set against the territory for a period and read against orders and pipeline in the reporting views. What counts towards a target, order value or collection, is agreed during setup.

items.q: What happens to open leads when a territory is redrawn?
items.a: They move to the new owner with their contacts, notes, visits and samples intact, so a reassignment does not restart the conversation. See lead management.

items.q: Does this help with coverage as well as sales?
items.a: Yes. Territory grouping is what makes a call cycle possible, because accounts due for a visit can be listed per patch. See beat plan software.
